elements.element: No obligation on Customer to disclose more favourable commercial offers received from third parties
elements.evidence: Section 7.2 ("Customer must disclose ... any more favourable commercial offer it receives") is deleted in its entirety (delete_paragraph p0026); rendered clause is empty.

elements.element: No obligation on Customer to match / grant Vendor a matching right before engaging another provider
elements.evidence: The words "Before engaging another provider ... and match for Vendor" no longer appear in the operative text.

elements.element: MFN pricing in Customer's favour remains permitted (no prohibition introduced)
elements.evidence: No new operative language was inserted; only deletion was performed, leaving Section 12.3's no-most-favoured-customer acknowledgement intact.

elements.element: MFN obligation limited to a defined product
elements.evidence: No MFN provision survives at all, so no product-scope limitation exists; the fallback bargain is not the structure delivered.
No duration term exists after deletion of Section 7.2.
No carve-out language present following deletion.

reasons: The preferred level is fully achieved: the entire disclose-and-match duty running against Customer is removed, leaving no MFN obligation on Customer and no matching right for Vendor.

Section 7.2 consisted of a single sentence that was wholly the offending MFN obligation, so deleting the paragraph changes nothing more than necessary; no narrower edit (operator, number, or short phrase) would eliminate the duty. The deterministic minimality gate flags whole-paragraph deletion generically, but here the paragraph and the offending obligation are coextensive.

No text was added, so no undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradiction is introduced; the deletion also removes the inconsistency with Section 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer made no most-favoured-customer commitment.

Fallback elements (defined product, 12-month term, reasonable-comparison carve-outs) are absent, but that is immaterial because the locked target level (preferred) is satisfied and the levels are not combined.
